title:
Eshu at the
Crossroads
description: Two friends swear that nothing can divide them, until a small god walks between them in a hat of two colours.

lines.text: Long ago, a red road ran between two compounds, and everyone who used it passed a crossroads.
Their gates opened on the same dust.
On that road lived two friends who farmed side by side and went to market as one.
They hoed together and ate from one bowl.
Every market morning they walked it together, talking the whole way.
They talked of rain and of prices.
They swore that nothing in the world could come between them. Not a quarrel. Not even a god.
People laughed. Old friends always say that.
One said it louder, for the road to hear.
Not even a god.
A small god was listening.
He smiled. He had been given work.
One bright day they set out as usual, each on his own side of the road.
Each carried a staff.
The crossroads came in sight.
At the crossroads, someone was waiting.
They took him for a post.
It was Eshu, a small god, the one who carries messages and mischief between heaven and earth.
A string of cowries rattled on his staff.
On his head sat a tall hat. One side of it was red. The other side was white.
ask: What was special about the hat?

lines.text: He said nothing.
He stepped onto the road and walked straight between the two friends.
He did not greet them. He did not stop. He went on, and the dust closed behind him.
Red dust hung in the air.
The left friend trusted his eyes.
The friend on the left said, what a fine red hat that was.
The right friend frowned.
The friend on the right stopped. He said, the hat was white.
Red, said the first.
White, said the second.
They stood in the road and argued, each sure the other had gone blind.
Each called the other a liar.
Neither crossed to the other's side.
By the time they reached the market, the quarrel had grown loud enough for the whole town to hear.
Sellers looked up from their goods.
They heard only each other.
Words became shouts, and shouts became a fight in the dust.
They rolled in the dust.
People left their stalls to watch two friends try to prove a colour.
The elders pulled them apart.
Still they would not agree.
That evening the town took them to the shrine, so the matter could be settled.
Half the town walked behind them, carrying torches.
Eshu was already there, sitting by the fire, and he was laughing.
The hat was still on his head.
He let them shout.
He lifted the hat and turned it slowly, once, so that every face could see.
White came round for the left friend.
Red came round for the right friend.
Red on one side. White on the other. Both friends had told the truth.
ask: How can the hat be both colours?

lines.text: The shrine went quiet.
Even the fire seemed to listen.
Eshu said, I walked between you, and each of you saw only the side you were given.
True, he said. Not the whole hat.
You forgot that you were still on the same road.
They were ashamed.
He set a calabash of palm wine between them.
Drink from one cup, he said.
The two friends looked at the hat, then at each other, and they laughed until they had to sit down.
The town laughed, and it was over.
By morning they were on the road again, walking as one.
One touched his own head, as if feeling for a hat, and smiled.
And that is why, at a crossroads, people still leave a little something for Eshu.
ask: What do people leave for Eshu?
